label: Guide me: Tax audit

params.name: lede
params.default: Work through an audit in {product}: is one needed, what moved against earlier years, GST against the books, the Form 3CD clauses and the Accounting Standards that apply, and the points still open.
params.label: lede

default.title: Pick the client
default.say: Choose the client; the year is picked at the top.

default.title: Is an audit needed?
default.say: From the turnover in the mapped books: above 1 crore for a business, 10 crore when cash is within 5%, 50 lakh for a profession, or presumptive with a lower profit. Tick what the books cannot show.

default.title: Against earlier years
default.say: Every mapped P&L and balance-sheet line against last year and up to four years before - from each year's statements, its filed return, or this year's previous-year column. Sharp moves are flagged, and so is a line that breaks its own history while turnover does not.

default.title: Raise a point
default.say: One click turns a flagged line into an audit point.

default.title: GST against the books
default.say: Add the GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 JSON from the GST portal - or the zip it downloads as. Month by month GSTR-3B against GSTR-1, and the year against the turnover in the books; a difference becomes an audit point.

default.title: Form 3CD checklist
default.say: Only the clauses that apply to this client, the riskiest first: pick the line of business, and clauses watching a flagged line rise to the top. Mark each one with a note; an issue opens an audit point.

default.title: Statutory audit
default.say: For a firm, LLP, AOP or proprietor: whether an LLP's accounts must be audited, the ICAI level from turnover and borrowings, and the Accounting Standards that apply at that level - each worked through like a clause.

default.title: Audit points
default.say: What still needs an answer before the report is signed, each with who answers it. A preparer raises points; a reviewer, auditor, partner or firm admin clears them.
